title: Square-root multiclass regret from Littlestone dimension
formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, for every pair of nonempty sets \(X,Y\), every nonempty class \(H\subseteq Y^X\) of Littlestone dimension at most \(d\), and all integers \(T\ge d\ge1\), the minimax expected regret satisfies \[R_T(H)\le C\sqrt{dT}?\] Infinite instance and label sets are allowed, and no regularity or computability restriction on the class is added. For the prediction game defined below, \[R_T(H)=\inf_A\ \sup_{(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_T,y_T)\in X\times Y}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^T(1-p_t(y_t))-\min_{h\in H}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{h(x_t)\ne y_t\}\right\}.\] Here \(p_t=A_t((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_{t-1},y_{t-1}),x_t)\) is a probability distribution on labels. The infimum ranges over all causal prediction rules, without computational restrictions.
why: Would determine whether Littlestone dimension alone controls the exact minimax cost of multiclass sequential prediction, beyond the already known learnability characterization.
status_note: The source’s 2023 universal multiclass conjecture is restored as the binary target. The sharper finite-label theorem is qualified by its explicitly stated minimax condition; Raman’s 2025 thesis retains the unrestricted binary issue. The checked May 2026 binary oracle result retains logarithmic factors, and no matching unrestricted multiclass resolution was found in the bounded search through 16 September 2026.

progress.text: The source proves general learnability and the unrestricted upper scale \(O(\sqrt{dT\log(eT/d)})\), compared with lower scale \(\Omega(\sqrt{dT})\), and poses the sharp square-root conjecture.
Its sharper finite-label upper bound \(O(\sqrt{\mathrm L(H)T\log|Y|})\) uses the additional minimax regularity condition specified in p. 9 footnote 4.
Raman’s dissertation repeats the qualification and states that the unrestricted binary square-root question remains open.

Targeted re-review corrected the omitted finite-label qualification, checked the source’s general theorem and exact game, and retained the previously authorized quantitative target. The bounded later-work search found no matching unrestricted multiclass resolution.

sentences: An online learner predicts a label and then observes the correct one.
Regret compares its expected mistakes with the best fixed hypothesis in hindsight.
Littlestone dimension measures the depth of binary prediction trees realizable by the class.
The question asks for a universal square-root dimension-times-horizon regret bound.
The constant cannot grow with the number of labels, even for infinite label spaces.

definitions: A hypothesis \(h\in H\) assigns a label from \(Y\) to each instance in \(X\). A depth-\(r\) Littlestone tree is a complete binary tree with an instance at each internal node and two distinct labels from \(Y\) on that node's outgoing edges; the pair of labels may vary by node. The tree is shattered if every root-to-leaf path has one fixed hypothesis agreeing with all its edge labels on its instance points. The dimension \(\mathrm L(H)\) is the largest shattered depth, or infinity if depths are unbounded. On each round the adversary presents \(x_t\), the learner supplies \(p_t\), and the adversary then reveals \(y_t\). The learner observes the actual label before the next round and is charged expected zero-one loss \(1-p_t(y_t)\). It does not observe future instances. The adversary may react to \(p_t\); loss is the displayed expectation, not a reaction to a sampled label. The sequence need not be realizable by any hypothesis. The comparator is one fixed hypothesis chosen in hindsight, whose minimum loss exists since the possible losses are integers from zero to \(T\). A distribution here is a function \(p:Y\to[0,1]\) satisfying \(\sum_{y\in Y}p(y)=1\), with this sum defined as the supremum of sums over finite subsets. It automatically has at most countable positive support. This atomic convention does not increase the best possible regret relative to arbitrary probability measures with measurable singletons: any missing atom mass can be assigned to one fixed label, increasing no zero-one loss. All histories and rules are arbitrary set functions, so no topology or measurability structure on \(X,H\) is required. Rules may know \(H\) and \(T\), need not be proper, and have no runtime, memory, computability or finite-description bound. Infima and suprema need not be attained. Dimension zero means all hypotheses agree pointwise and zero regret is attainable. The range \(T\ge d\) avoids the separate saturation regime because cumulative regret cannot exceed \(T\). All requested comparison constants must be independent of the instance and label spaces, class, dimension and horizon.
answer_criterion: Give a complete, mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the displayed assertion or of its logical negation, with exactly the stated model, quantifier order and parameter dependence. A bound for a restricted subclass or one particular algorithm is insufficient to refute a universal existence assertion. Determining the entire optimal rate or a numerical approximation to it is not required.

context_blocks.text: The learner sees the current instance and then receives the correct label after predicting. It can distribute its prediction among labels, and is scored by expected mistakes relative to the best fixed hypothesis. Labels can contradict every member of the class. The regret target is therefore different from a realizable mistake bound.

The 2023 paper proves that finite Littlestone dimension characterizes agnostic multiclass online learnability even for unbounded label spaces. This general learnability theorem does not require the separate minimax regularity assumption used in its sharper finite-label result. The remaining rate question asks how far a learner must fall behind the best fixed concept.

The unrestricted argument in §3 gives regret at most \(\mathrm L(H)+\sqrt{(T/2)\mathrm L(H)\ln(eT/\mathrm L(H))}\) for positive dimension. In the stated horizon range this yields \(R(d,T)=O(\sqrt{dT\log(eT/d)})\). A universal lower scale is \(\Omega(\sqrt{dT})\). The logarithm is part of the unresolved gap and cannot be suppressed when asking for constant factors.

For a finite label set, Theorem 9 gives \(O(\sqrt{\mathrm L(H)T\log|Y|})\) under the additional minimax regularity condition explicitly stated in p. 9 footnote 4 for those results. Under that condition a fixed label count yields the square-root scale, but the coefficient grows with the count. Even for two labels, removing the condition for unrestricted classes is a separate open issue recorded by the source and by the 2025 thesis.

The binary question restores the source’s square-root upper-bound conjecture. It retains arbitrary instance and label sets and does not add the regularity condition used in some sharper special-case theorems. The known lower scale motivates this endpoint; a complete determination of an alternative rate is not required.

The checked May 2026 oracle-complexity paper concerns binary classification and retains logarithmic factors in its dimension-dependent regret statement. It improves resource use within an online algorithm and does not resolve the unrestricted multiclass constant-factor rate.
